anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level SQL or transaction design forces the engine to process more data, rows, or time than functionally required.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine runtime settings for memory, logging, parallelism, and background workers are mis-tuned relative to hardware, workload mix, or version defaults.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupted, making access paths and stored rows unreliable.

When all three conditions coexist, the system exhibits a tangled set of symptoms: long-running statements and transactions that repeatedly hit slow-query thresholds; erratic latency where the same query alternates between slow execution, errors, or silent mis-reads; spikes in I/O, CPU spin, or log-write waits that do not match actual hardware utilization; surges of checkpoint, auto-vacuum, or page-verification activity; duplicate or missing rows returned by heavy scans; sudden fallback to full table scans despite available indexes; repeated application retries that amplify load; and intermittent corruption errors or crash-recovery events that escalate under peak workload periods.

Causally, inefficient SQL drives excessive scans, joins, and long transactions, multiplying the physical touch-rate on pages that already contain latent corruption. Misaligned configuration—such as undersized buffer pools, over-aggressive checkpoint intervals, or disabled verification settings—both magnifies the performance cost of the bloated workload and increases churn on the compromised storage blocks. The heavier I/O and checkpoint storms induced by poor SQL and bad parameters accelerate exposure of damaged pages, which in turn trigger retries, error handling paths, and emergency maintenance workers; these extra activities further inflate resource contention created by the original workload logic. Meanwhile, corruption-induced plan instability forces the optimizer to abandon indexes, deepening the performance penalty of the already inefficient queries. The feedback loop among inefficient SQL, misconfiguration, and structural corruption therefore degrades throughput, inflates tail latency, and jeopardizes data correctness across both transactional and analytical usage.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits longer than net_write_timeout while writing a block to the client connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
